fixed.problem: An uploaded flow file is untrusted, but to_conn() used int(...) and flow['src_addr'] with no checks, and read_flows() caught only JSONDecodeError. If the first line was a valid flow and any later line was damaged, POST /api/analyses returned HTTP 500. Reproduced with TestClient for six cases: bytes "abc", dst_port [1], bytes 1e400, bytes 2**70, a 100,000-deep [[[...]]] line (RecursionError) and time_flow_start_ns 10**40. src_addr null or a dict was stored as the address (200).
fixed.fix: Added whole_number() (a JSON int from 0 to 2**63-1; ports up to 65535; ICMP type and code up to 255) and ip_text() (a str that ipaddress parses). to_zeek_logs() skips a record that raises ValueError or RecursionError, the same way it skips a half-written line. read_flows() now catches ValueError and RecursionError. All eight hostile uploads now return 200 and keep the good records. Also softened the v5 ICMP comment to 'the usual exporter convention'.

fixed.problem: requests trusts the environment by default. Tested: with HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 the upload went to that proxy (ProxyError), so the captures and token would leave through a proxy (rule 1). A ~/.netrc entry for the console host replaced 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' with 'Basic YWxpY2U6c2VjcmV0', which sent the netrc password to the console and broke ingest.
fixed.fix: Added console_session(): a requests.Session with trust_env = False. upload() and upload_finished() take session=None and use it by default. Tests can still pass a TestClient. Added test_upload_ignores_proxy_settings_and_netrc.

fixed.problem: tcpdump runs the whole -w name through strftime (tcpdump.c MakeFilename, tcpdump-4.99 branch), so a '%' in spool_dir would be expanded.
fixed.fix: tcpdump_command() writes the folder with '%' replaced by '%%'. Added test_percent_in_the_spool_folder_is_not_a_time_pattern.

fixed.problem: main() created spool_dir as root (the agent runs under sudo). tcpdump -Z opens its output files only after dropping to capture_user (tcpdump.1.in, -Z), so with a folder the agent had just created, tcpdump could not write and exited. main() still returned 0.
fixed.fix: Added prepare_spool(): a folder the agent creates on Linux or macOS as root is chown'ed to capture_user. An existing folder is never changed. run_tcpdump() returns tcpdump's exit code and main() returns it. Added test_spool_folder_the_agent_creates_goes_to_capture_user.

fixed.problem: --upload-only uses capture_running=False, so it also uploads and moves the file tcpdump is still writing if the agent's capture is running. Its help text did not say this.
fixed.fix: Help text now says to use it only while the agent is stopped. Also added a docstring line, checked against pktmon-start.md: pktmon's default log mode is circular with a 512 MB file, so a very busy interval loses its oldest packets.

fixed.problem: Three mutations survived: removing sort_keys from the uid hash, accepting any JSON line that has src_addr (no type check), and removing the time_received fallback when the flow times are missing.
fixed.fix: Added test_uid_does_not_depend_on_the_order_of_the_fields, test_sflow_and_other_json_with_src_addr_are_not_flows and test_flow_without_flow_times_uses_the_receive_time. Also added test_damaged_records_are_skipped_not_fatal and test_icmp_type_and_code_must_fit_in_a_byte. All three mutations are now caught.

fixed.problem: The notes did not describe the review fixes. They implied the user must make the spool folder writable by capture_user by hand.
fixed.fix: Added a 'Review fixes' section with the reproduced failures and what changed.

findings.problem: Head-of-line blocking: upload_finished() breaks on any status other than 2xx, 400 or 413 and retries the oldest file first. A capture the console always answers with 422 (ZeekError/SuricataError on that file) or 500 blocks every later upload forever. With 401 or 404 (wrong token, ingest off), the whole oldest file is re-sent every CHECK_EVERY=10 s, and spool_dir grows without limit.
findings.suggestion: Lead decision. Options: count attempts per file and move it to rejected/ after N tries; treat 422 as rejected if ZeekError cannot be transient; or back off exponentially and stop on 401/404 with a clear message. Also add a spool size limit (oldest unsent files deleted, with a log line).

findings.problem: requests builds the whole multipart body in memory (requests/models.py _encode_files: fdata = fp.read()). Each upload therefore holds the whole capture file in RAM on the host (up to the console's 1 GiB limit).
findings.suggestion: Fine for 15-minute home captures. If large files are expected, stream the upload (requests-toolbelt MultipartEncoder is a new dependency and needs approval) or lower rotate_seconds.

findings.problem: finished_files() holds back the newest file by NAME. If the clock goes back (no RTC, NTP correction), a leftover file from an earlier run can sort after the file tcpdump is writing. That file would then be uploaded and moved while still open. run_pktmon() never converts .etl files left by a crash. A failing pktmon start or etl2pcap ends the agent with a traceback.
findings.suggestion: Optionally also hold back the most recently modified file, and convert leftover capture-*.etl at startup. Document as not run on Windows.

findings.problem: read_flows() iterates text lines with no length limit. One giant line (up to the 1 GiB upload limit) is read into memory before json.loads. The NetFlow v5 ICMP decoding (type*256+code in dst_port) and the possible same convention in NetFlow v9 templates without ICMP_TYPE still lack a primary source. goflow2 docs/protocols.md shows icmp_type/icmp_code are not filled for v5. For v9 and IPFIX without the ICMP field, the adapter reports type 0 / code 0.
findings.suggestion: Accept the memory bound (the same as the Zeek log adapters) or read with a per-line cap. Ask the lead to soften the ICMP sentence in the guide or find a Cisco or IETF source. A dst_port fallback for v9 and IPFIX was not added because no primary source supports it.

findings.problem: (Not the builder's file.) run_pipeline's 400 message does not mention goflow2 flow files, and pick_adapter's UnsupportedInput text in pipeline.py says only 'pcap/pcapng file or a Zeek log folder/archive'. Before the netflow.py fix, damaged flow uploads returned an unhandled 500.
findings.suggestion: Lead: add 'or a goflow2 NetFlow/IPFIX JSON file' to both messages. If the lead wants another layer of defence, run_pipeline could map unexpected ValueError to 400.

findings.problem: trust_env=False also ignores REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE. An https console_url with a self-signed certificate therefore cannot be trusted through the environment. Port 8001 is plain HTTP, so the token crosses the LAN unencrypted (the builder already noted this).
findings.suggestion: If TLS on the ingest port is adopted, add an explicit ca_file setting to agent.toml and pass verify=<ca_file>.
